cards.explanation: The answer is that a gentle answer turns away wrath. Solomon says, "A gentle answer turns away wrath…" and the heat leaves the room. The angry person still has feelings, but nobody tossed fresh logs on the fire. Soft words are a quiet kind of strong, friends.

The answer is in every place. The verse says, "The eyes of the LORD are in every place, observing the evil and the good." No spot is left out, not even a quiet corner. The verse puts no limit on where, friends. And what He observes is both the evil and the good.

The answer is crushes. The verse says "…a perverse tongue crushes the spirit." Look at the two sides of it, bakers: a soothing tongue is a tree of life, and a perverse one flattens a person. Words are heavier than they look.

The answer is prudent. The verse says, "…whoever heeds correction is prudent." Prudent just means careful and wise. The person who listens when somebody says "hey, try it this way" ends up on the smart side of the verse, friends.
The answer is False. The verse says "The lips of the wise spread knowledge, but not so the hearts of fools." Knowledge-spreading belongs to the wise side, friends. The fool's heart doesn't do it.

The answer is detestable. The verse says, "The sacrifice of the wicked is detestable to the LORD, but the prayer of the upright is His delight." Look at who's holding what, bakers: a sacrifice is something you bring, a prayer is something you say, and the verse says the one who brings it matters. Plot twist, right? Then verse 9 says it about whole lives: "The LORD detests the way of the wicked, but He loves those who pursue righteousness."
The answer is loves. The verse says, "…He loves those who pursue righteousness." Notice the word pursue, friends, which means they're chasing it. And the LORD loves the ones who go after it.

The answer is False. The verse says, "Sheol and Abaddon lie open before the LORD—how much more the hearts of men!" Those two lie open before Him. So the "…how much more…" tells you hearts are no harder for Him to see, friends. Nothing in there is hidden from Him.

The answer is a cheerful face. The verse says, "A joyful heart makes a cheerful countenance…" Countenance is just a fancy word for your face. What's going on inside tends to show up on the outside, bakers, like when I smell a fresh batch and my whole mustache lifts.

The answer is True. The verse says "All the days of the oppressed are bad, but a cheerful heart has a continual feast." It puts the two side by side, friends. I'd take the continual feast, and I'm saying that as a guy with a whole bakery.

The answer is hatred. The verse says, "Better a dish of vegetables where there is love than a fattened ox with hatred." A fattened ox is a fancy meal, and it still loses to a plain dish with love at the table. The verse calls the dish of vegetables where there is love the better one, friends.

The answer is True. The verse says, "A hot-tempered man stirs up strife, but he who is slow to anger calms dispute." One person adds fuel and the other takes it away. The verse puts them side by side, bakers, and the results go opposite ways. Being slow to anger is quiet work, but it does calm things down.

The answer is False. The verse says, "A wise son brings joy to his father, but a foolish man despises his mother." The question swapped in "honors," but the verse says despises. That's a big difference in one word, friends.

The answer is joy, and it's a sneaky one. "Folly is joy to one who lacks judgment…" Someone without judgment actually enjoys the silly choices, bakers. Meanwhile the man of understanding walks a straight path.

The answer is they succeed. The verse says, "Plans fail for lack of counsel, but with many advisers they succeed." It puts failure on the side of lacking counsel and success on the side of many advisers. So the verse points you toward asking around, friends. One more voice in the kitchen never hurt a batch.
The answer is upward. "The path of life leads upward for the wise, that he may avoid going down to Sheol." Up for the wise, and the verse sets that against going down. The direction matters, bakers.

The answer is widow. The verse says, "The LORD tears down the house of the proud, but He protects the boundaries of the widow." A widow is a woman whose husband has died. The verse says it's her boundaries He protects, friends. The proud get their house torn down, and she gets her boundaries protected.
The answer is False. The verse says "He who is greedy for unjust gain brings trouble on his household…" So it isn't only on himself, friends. The whole house feels it.

The answer is that the heart of the righteous ponders how to answer. The verse says, "The heart of the righteous ponders how to answer, but the mouth of the wicked blurts out evil." The righteous heart does its thinking first, bakers. That's the opposite of blurting.

The answer is far from. The verse says, "The LORD is far from the wicked, but He hears the prayer of the righteous." That's a heavy line, friends, and the verse doesn't soften it. Then it turns on a dime to the prayer of the righteous. I'd rather be on the hearing side of that verse.

The answer is False. The verse says, "He who ignores discipline despises himself, but whoever heeds correction gains understanding." Ignoring discipline doesn't protect him, friends. The verse puts the two side by side, and the one who heeds correction gains understanding.

The answer is humility. The chapter closes with "The fear of the LORD is the instruction of wisdom, and humility comes before honor." Humility is named first and honor comes after it, bakers. Honor doesn't get to cut the line. That's the order the verse sets.
